reasoning:
The story first. NVIDIA is the arms dealer of the AI build-out: it sells the most capable accelerated-computing silicon and systems, and it has wrapped that hardware in a software ecosystem (CUDA) and a networking stack that lock customers in. Who buys? The hyperscalers, sovereigns, and increasingly every enterprise standing up AI infrastructure. Is it defensible? For now, yes, though the very customers writing the checks are the ones funding alternatives. That tension is the whole valuation question.

Connecting the story to numbers. Revenue was $216B last fiscal year, and the Street sees roughly $391B this year and $552B next, so I anchor the near term to those visible orders, then fade growth from the low-80s percent down to a terminal 4% over a ten-year explicit period. Operating margin starts at the current elite 60% and eases toward a still-extraordinary 48-49% as competition and customer silicon press on price. Tax normalizes to 16%, and because this is a fabless, capital-light business, capex and D&A both run near 3% of revenue, so reinvestment is light and free cash flow conversion is high.

The risk piece is where I part company with the bulls, and it is the crux. Cost of equity is rf plus beta times ERP. The risk-free rate is 4.4%, the equity risk premium 5.5%, and the regression beta is 2.20. I will not sand that down to 1.3 the way a sell-side model might; this stock genuinely moves about twice the market and a fair discount rate has to reflect that. Using a beta of 2.0, cost of equity is 15.4%, and with a trivial debt weight the WACC is about 15.3%. Terminal growth I cap at the risk-free rate, 4%, since no company grows faster than the economy forever.

The math says intrinsic value near $132 per share on the base case, roughly 36% below the $205 price. The bull path (beta 1.65, sustained 50%-plus growth) gets to about $244; the bear (beta 2.2, harder fade) to roughly $65. My cross-check: NVDA trades at about 34x trailing EV/EBITDA and 23x EV/sales, both well above the AI-semi peer median once you exclude the extreme small-caps, so the relative lens does not rescue the intrinsic gap; if anything it confirms a full price. Connecting it all: this is a magnificent business at a cost of capital its own volatility demands, and at that honest discount rate the price already discounts a near-flawless decade. Bearish on value, with full respect for the franchise.
